claims.source: 10 U.S.C. Sec. 119, Special access programs: congressional oversight
claims.text: 10 U.S.C. 119 requires congressional notification of special access programmes but permits the Secretary of Defense to waive that notification for a programme, reporting instead only to the chairs and ranking members of the defence committees.
50 U.S.C. 3510 permits certain intelligence expenditures to be accounted for solely on the certificate of the agency head, with that certificate deemed a sufficient voucher.

claims.source: DoD Directive 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy
claims.text: DoD Directive 5205.07 establishes the policy framework for acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived special access programmes and assigns the approval authority.

connections.label: Executive Policy & Directives
connections.note: DoDD 5205.07 is the directive-layer implementation of authority that derives from executive order rather than statute.

connections.edgeLabel: Statutory basis for the access tier
connections.label: Special Access Programs
connections.note: 10 U.S.C. 119 and DoDD 5205.07 are the legal and policy instruments that create the special access programme category; the SAP domain is the applied form of the secrecy-law domain.

connections.edgeLabel: Fixes the three categories and takes classification authority away from 28 agencies
connections.label: Executive Order 10501 - Safeguarding Official Information in the Interests of the Defense of the United States (5 November 1953)
connections.note: Section 1 bars any designation other than Top Secret, Secret and Confidential 'except as expressly provided by statute'. Section 2 provides that agencies without direct national-defense responsibility have no original classification authority at all, and the attached memorandum names 28 of them.

sources.name: EO 10501 secs. 1 and 2 and attached memorandum

connections.edgeLabel: Authorises reclassification after a disclosure request
connections.label: Executive Order 12356 - National Security Information (2 April 1982)
connections.note: Section 1.6(c) permits reclassifying information 'previously declassified and disclosed' where it is determined in writing that it needs protection and 'may reasonably be recovered'; 1.6(d) permits classification or reclassification after a FOIA, Privacy Act or mandatory-review request has been received.

connections.edgeLabel: One of the three statutory layers of the secrecy architecture
connections.label: Invention Secrecy Act of 1951 (Pub. L. 82-256, 66 Stat. 3), codified at 35 U.S.C. 181-188
connections.note: The domain description already names this Act as one of the three statutory layers of the secrecy architecture and the board carried no node for it.

sources.name: 35 U.S.C. 181, Secrecy of certain inventions and withholding of patent

connections.edgeLabel: Compartment created by bypassing the review committee, in writing
connections.label: Project BLUEBIRD
connections.note: The proposal states on its face that it goes directly to the Director rather than through the Projects Review Committee because of the project's sensitivity, and asks that knowledge be held to the absolute minimum number of persons.

connections.label: DoD Nuclear Weapon Personnel Reliability Program (DoD Directive 5210.42)
connections.note: The board's suppression argument usually runs through classification; PRP is the administrative alternative, a published rule that can remove a person from his job without any classification decision at all.

desc: Everything this board describes is, on its face, legal - and that is the point. Classification authority flows from executive order rather than statute for most national security information, which means the same executive branch that runs a programme also decides whether Congress and the courts may learn of it. Layered on top are the Atomic Energy Act's 'born classified' Restricted Data regime, the Invention Secrecy Act's power to impose secrecy orders on patent applications, and 50 U.S.C. 3510's authority for unvouchered and confidential expenditure certified by agency heads rather than audited. The dual-use route into a concealment programme is simple and requires no conspiracy: an activity placed inside a special access programme, then waived from ordinary congressional notification under the exception in 10 U.S.C. 119, is protected by exactly the same machinery whether it holds a stealth aircraft or a recovered craft, and the machinery cannot tell the difference. Scoring high on this domain means an entity is a wielder of classification authority - an original classification authority, a security officer, a programme security manager - rather than a person subject to it.
